SMTO-SCH-0026 — The Agent tried to wait instead of scheduling your later task

GUID: 7fe9f787-f086-46f7-ac0b-1613eb66b2d8
Slug: future-work-requires-schedule
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • Your task is meant to run at a later time, so it needs a saved schedule that keeps working even if this conversation ends. The Agent tried to just wait inside this run, and SMTO stopped that.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep the conversation open. The Agent is told to create a schedule for your task instead of waiting. A saved schedule still runs at the right time even after this run has finished.
  2. Open Schedules and check that a schedule for this task shows the right Next run time. This confirms the task was actually saved for later.
  3. If no schedule appears and the run has stopped, select New schedule and set the task and time yourself. The schedule editor creates the same kind of saved schedule directly.

What success looks like

  • One schedule for your task appears on the Schedules page with the time you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off the Enforce temporal routing check to get past this; it could make the Agent act at the wrong time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Temporal routing blocked wait_for_event for a pending future-independent task, which must be created as a durable schedule instead of an in-run wait.

What this means

  • A pending future-independent task is sent to wait_for_event instead of the durable schedule-creation route. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • A pending future-independent task is sent to wait_for_event instead of the durable schedule-creation route.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare captured route kind and proposed tool rather than using a local timer for independent scheduled work.

How to fix it

  • temporal_routing.guard found phase pending_schedule for a future_independent route and a proposed wait_for_event. Call schedule.create with the captured expected instruction and timing (the correction includes the expected fields); an in-run wait does not replace a durable future task.
  • Create the intended durable schedule with the captured future-task instruction and timing. An in-run wait does not replace a durable future task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported durable schedule captures the exact intended instruction and timing.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
